Evidence caveats

  • 15,276 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 15,276 games at 64.7%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. Evidence caveats

  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.

Evidence caveats

  • 462 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 462 games at 63.0%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

Evidence caveats

  • 30 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 30 games at 76.7%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

Evidence caveats

  • 1,212 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 1,212 games at 70.5%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.

Evidence caveats

  • 20,364 older or lineage-incompatible Showdown games are shown as legacy context only and are excluded from the evidence grade.
  • KO, damage, opener, and fast-matchup findings come from the approximate simulator. The bench-favored-versus-contributing table is artifact-scoped current Showdown evidence when available; the two populations are labelled with their own denominators because their bring and win rates measure different experiments.
  • Matchup playbooks describe what the field policy repeatedly selected against each opponent. They do not claim the most-used bring or lead causally outperforms alternatives.
  • Bring-versus-bench rates are observational and matchup-selected. A negative lift can mean a Pokémon is reserved for the hardest matchups, not that it is intrinsically harmful.
  • Legacy exact context: 20,364 games at 63.7%; excluded from the headline and evidence grade.
